newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds turn higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds turn higher on short-covering.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Friday as a bout of short-covering in the afternoon turned earlier losses into gains.
"There was a bit of short-covering," said a trader at a local bank. Activity remained subdued, however, with end-users absent.
"It was all a game between traders," added the trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/8 to 90-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.35 to 126.65.
Like this week, the coming sessions will be "all about expectations about the direction of U.S. Treasuries," said another trader.
That is especially so as the policy-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets March 25 to decided on monetary policy.

And the ongoing uncertainty in the run up to the meeting will continue as "it is difficult to say whether a hike in U.S. rates has been discounted by either U.S. or Argentine markets," said the second trader.
Call money rates fell to 5.88 percent from 5.93 percent.
